extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/applicants submitting grant applications to NLM/NIH
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and FAQ about how NLM/NIH peer review and funding decisions are made, what scores and criteria mean, reviewer selection, and the appeal process for grant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are chosen primarily for their subject domain expertise; most also have considerable experience with the NIH granting process. The majority of NLM applications are reviewed by the BILDS Review Committee; some are reviewed by Special Emphasis Panels (SEPs). A second level review is performed by NLM's Board of Regents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' subject-matter fit and NIH review experience drive selection. Some applications may go to ad hoc SEPs. Expect a second-level (Council/Board of Regents) review after peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-to-fund factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to fund any given grant is made by the Institute Director based on scientific merit (as reflected by the priority score), relevance to the NLM mission, recommendations of the NLM Board of Regents (Council) and availability of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a good impact/priority score does not guarantee funding — relevance to NLM priorities, Board recommendations, portfolio balance, and available funds also determine awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: In a cover letter you may suggest areas of expertise for reviewers that might best fit the subject area covered by your application. It is not appropriate to suggest specific experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide topical/expertise guidance rather than names; do so in the cover letter accompanying your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (NIH core review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance — one of the general criteria established by NIH for evaluating an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The importance assigned to each criterion varies depending on the funding mechanism and program area. Each funding opportunity announcement lists the criteria that will be used to judge the merit of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (NIH core review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) — one of the general criteria established by NIH for evaluating an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the qualifications, experience, and suitability of the investigators for the proposed work; relative weight depends on funding mechanism and program area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (NIH core review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation — one of the general criteria established by NIH for evaluating an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses novelty of concepts, approaches or methods. Note: innovation is not a requirement of resource grants; importance varies by mechanism and announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (NIH core review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach — one of the general criteria established by NIH for evaluating an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines the rigor and feasibility of the proposed methods and analyses. Weight varies with mechanism; detailed methodological concerns commonly drive critiques and score guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (NIH core review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment — one of the general criteria established by NIH for evaluating an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates institutional support, available resources, and whether the setting will contribute to project success; importance depends on funding mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact/Priority score (overall impact metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: After discussing an application, members of the review group privately vote a numerical impact/priority score from 1 to 9 (1 is best). The final overall impact score = average of members’ impact scores × 10, resulting in a score from 10 to 90 (10 is best). NLM uses the overall Impact Score as the primary basis for award decisions on all grant types, along with innovation and potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical fundable thresholds at NLM: experienced investigators — Impact scores ~30 or better most likely to be funded; Early Stage/New Investigators and K award applicants — Impact scores of 35 or better will be considered. All awards are subject to availability of funds; specific fundable ranges may be set for other grant types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion scores (per-core-criterion metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assign a criterion score from 1 to 9 (1 is best) to each core NIH review criterion (significance, investigator, innovation, approach, and environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores are provided to assist applicants in understanding strengths and weaknesses. Criterion scores are not used to calculate the final impact/priority score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 4 weeks after review, a written evaluation called the Summary Statement is posted in eRA Commons. It is compiled by the Scientific Review Officer (SRO) and contains written critiques prepared by assigned reviewers and recommendations regarding budget and human subject considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application received full discussion, the Summary Statement also includes a resume and summary of the discussion written by the SRO. Log into eRA Commons to view/download the Summary Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional documentation when application is under consideration for funding
rubrics_metrics.description: If applications with impact/priority scores fall within the fundable range, NLM's Grants Management staff will request additional documentation: updated 'other support' for key participants; the status of Institutional Review Board action; and certification that key personnel have received training in the protection of human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This request for additional information indicates the application is under consideration but is not an award notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget adjustment considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: After review, reviewers may recommend that elements of your budget be reduced. NLM Program staff may also reduce the budget for programmatic reasons or because available funds are not sufficient to provide full funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget reductions can come from peer review recommendations or programmatic/fund-availability decisions at NLM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal process timing and formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is a written communication that must be: received after issuance of the summary statement and up to 30 calendar days after the second level of peer review; describe a flaw or perceived flaw in the review process for a particular application; be based on one or more allowable issues; and display concurrence from the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal letters must be submitted to the Program Official (PO). The PO will acknowledge receipt within 10 days. Appeals submitted before the summary statement or later than 30 days after the Council meeting will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable issues for appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals will be considered only if based on one or more of the following process issues: evidence of bias by one or more reviewers; conflict of interest as specified in 42 CFR 52h.5; lack of appropriate expertise within the Scientific Review Group (SRG); factual error(s) by one or more reviewers that could have altered the review outcome substantially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals based solely on differences of scientific opinion will not be accepted. A letter that does not meet these criteria or lacks AOR concurrence will be treated as a grievance and handled by IC-specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on contacting reviewers or Council members
rubrics_metrics.description: At no time should the PD/PI or an official of the applicant organization attempt to contact individual members of the Scientific Review Group (SRG) or the Council to discuss the review of an application or appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such contact could jeopardize the confidentiality of the review process and is explicitly disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal outcomes and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Only two outcomes are possible following Council consideration of an appeal: Council may concur with the appeal and recommend re-review; or Council may concur with the SRG's recommendation and deny the appeal. The recommendation of Council concerning resolution of an appeal is final and will not be considered again by the NIH through this or another process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If re-review is recommended, the original application (without additional materials) will be re-reviewed by the same or a different SRG; the re-review outcome is final and not subject to further appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of impact scores and where to view them
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact scores are typically available within a few days after review; log into your NIH eRA Commons PI account to see your score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions are provided on how to view impact/priority scores and Summary Statements in eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification policy for unfunded applications
rubrics_metrics.description: No notifications are sent to grant applicants whose applications did not receive funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure about funding status, applicants should contact the appropriate NLM program officer listed in the grant program announcement.
